title: Servo: Robots and Mechs Sound Effects
shortText: 106 robot SFX: four ladders (footsteps by weight, power, alert, damage) plus servos, sparks and sensors. WAV + OGG.
html:
A robot body your game can drive

106 robot and mech sound effects built around four ladders: the footsteps land heavier, the power core brightens, the alert beeps faster and the malfunction runs longer, one rung at a time. Wire size, power, threat or damage to a rung and the sound follows.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 23 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. One take of every footstep rung, all 5 power loops and all 5 alert loops, the shortest and the longest malfunction, a servo sweep with every take, a target lock, an armour hit and the assembly line loop.

Four ladders, one number each

A robot is a set of numbers: how heavy it is, how much power it has, how alarmed it is, how broken it is. Each ladder is a set of files named by rung (_t1 to _t5), so your game picks the rung from a number it already has.

  • Footsteps by weight: 5 weight classes from a small walker to a titan, a steel foot striking with the weight landing under it, darker and heavier at every rung. Three takes each.
  • Power level: 5 seamless power core loops, a low steel hum with the air over it opening up at every rung. Crossfade between rungs.
  • Alert: 5 seamless loops of a double beep, from 30 to 95 beeps a minute (one every 2.00 s down to 0.63 s) as the threat rises.
  • Malfunction: 5 bursts of sparks and a stuttering motor, longer at every rung as the damage builds. Two takes each.

Checked from the shipped files, not promised: all 16 steps between rungs move the declared way (at least 8% in brightness on the footsteps and the power core, 12% in length on the alert and the malfunction), and every ladder spans at least 1.5 times end to end. Failing steps: 0.

The robot around them

23 sounds for one robot, 66 files, every one with takes so the same servo never plays twice in a row:

  • Servos and joints: a quick servo snap, a slow arm sweep and a servo straining under load (each whine rising as the joint moves and settling as it arrives), a joint ratcheting through its detents, a gripper clamping shut, a hydraulic piston.
  • Power: booting up, a capacitor charging, powering down to a last clunk, an overheating vent.
  • Damage: a shower of sparks, a short circuit, a heavy round off armour plate, a robot falling apart.
  • Sensors: a scan sweep, a target lock, a target lost, a drone passing overhead.
  • Stingers and interface: an activation (power drawn in, a heavy hit and a ring of steel), a system failure, and a small menu set.
  • 5 ambience loops: a factory floor, a power core in its housing, a hovering drone, a server room and an assembly line.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file.
  • 15 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 33 variation sets whose takes are separate renders, never one file re pitched.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.21 dB, so a titan's footstep and a menu tick share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 978 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised sounds designed for games, not field recordings. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No robot voices, no weapons fire, no vehicles and nothing musical: a beep is one struck tone, never a tune.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Ship Systems, sci fi interface and machinery: the terminals and the ship around your robot.
  • Escapement, clockwork, brass and the machine room: the gears before the servos.
  • Haulage, vehicles, motors and industrial machines: the heavy plant on the same factory floor.
